decisions.final:
Pour tout pt $x$ de $D$, l'ens des ``branches'' de $D$ passant par $x$ est un ensemble fini. $I(x)$, Par définition, les \uline{germes} \inserted{en $x$} \uline{de sous-multiplicités} \uuline{attaché\unsure{s|es}} \uuline{à $D$} sont les intersections d'un nb fini \deleted{de} parmi les $D_{x,i}\in I(x)$.
\margin{il vaut mieux prendre un $x\in X$, et poser $I(x)=\phi$ si $x\notin D$.}
Ces \unsure{germes} forment un ensemble ordonné \inserted{$\Delta_x\unsure{=(|(=}\Delta_x(X\unsure{,D}))$} antiisomorphe \unsure{à|:} $\mathcal P(I(x))$, \deleted{Si \unsure{$J$ est}}\inserted{la codimension} \deleted{\unsure{une|avec|ceux}} de $D_{x,J}$ $(J\subset I(x))$ étant donnée par
\[
(149)\qquad \operatorname{Codim}(D_{x,J},X_x)=\operatorname{card}J
\]
\margin{105}
decisions.ink: The same x, D, I(x), branch expression, Delta subscript and subset-condition objects are present under both math-delimiter conventions; those wrapper differences supply no new source glyph. The D is internally crossed/retraced, but the extra strokes remain within its body. No independent strike or separately bounded earlier letter is exposed, so a definite cancellation state is not established. One line runs under the baseline germes/de and continues under sous-multiplicités. The en x is above it with a separate curved attachment guide, and has no underline of its own. The blind enclosing underline would incorrectly include that insertion. The a/t/t/a/c/h/é sequence is visible. The final low group is compressed and does not expose a separate extra e with certainty. Both underline strokes are independent and clear. The note occupies four oblique marginal baselines. Moving its wrapper to the end is a serialization choice, not new prose. The following sentence begins with an open capital C and low e/s, not a tall L or lowercase l. The g descender and opening low sequence remain visible, but the final low bodies are heavily retraced. Germes remains the candidate; no separately bounded cancelled word after it is inferred. Two Delta triangles, x subscripts, equality and X are exposed. The opening curve overlaps equality and the second Delta; at the right edge the comma-D tail is cramped, and two closing curves remain visible. The blind shorter formula would discard one of those curves and the unresolved opening stroke. There are two small separate marks before P. The lower mark does not expose a complete a loop, so the accent-plus-a and colon interpretations remain possible. The S curve and dotted i are traceable despite the crossing line. The J/est sequence is obscured by the strike and raised replacement, so the first narrower doubt is retained. The heavy line crosses nearly all low bodies. Small rounded/arched remnants support tentative short-word candidates but do not certify the sequence or word length; cancellation itself is certain. The first word includes an extended low a/n run before the tall final t; it is longer than est and its strokes remain exposed. Donnée has a tall initial d, connected middle arches and two short final e-like bodies before the separate p descender of par. The feminine ending is read from those bodies. The initial open C is appreciably taller than o/i/m and than the lowercase c in card on the same display. Case is not regularized. The rotated note shows a small loop crossed by a very long stem, extending markedly below it, rather than a short slash through an oval. A separate final point follows D. The four lines remain a margin note; dollar versus parenthesized math and its placement in the serialized prose do not change the reading.
